## Purpose

This SOP describes the deployment, programming, data retrieval, and
maintenance of Onset HOBO pendant and MX-series data loggers used for
unattended monitoring of air temperature, relative humidity, and light
intensity at EA Program field sites. These compact loggers provide
continuous microclimatic data for characterizing site conditions,
supporting ecological studies, and supplementing manual weather
observations [@onset_hobou23; @wmo_guide2018].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** HOBO Pendant MX2201, MX2202 (temperature/light),
  HOBO MX2301 (temperature/RH), HOBO Pendant UA-002 (temperature/
  light, legacy), and similar Onset loggers deployed at EA Program
  field sites
- **Does not apply to:** HOBO water level loggers (see
  [SOP-F203](SOP-F203-hobo-water-level-transducers.qmd)); fixed,
  permanently installed weather stations managed by other departments;
  air quality sensors (see
  [SOP-F502](SOP-F502-air-quality-portable-sensors.qmd))
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve deployment plan and logging interval            |
| Trained Personnel | Deploy, retrieve, and download loggers per this SOP     |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use                |


## Definitions

- **Bluetooth logging:** A wireless communication protocol used by
  MX-series HOBO loggers; enables programming and data download via
  the HOBOconnect smartphone app without cables; requires proximity
  (typically within 15 m of the logger) [@onset_hobou23].
- **Data gap:** A period within a logger deployment during which no
  data were recorded; caused by battery failure, logger reset, or
  memory overflow; must be documented in the project data log.
- **HOBOconnect:** The Onset smartphone app (iOS and Android) used to
  program, launch, and download data from Bluetooth-enabled MX-series
  HOBO loggers; requires the logger to be within Bluetooth range
  [@onset_hoboware].
- **HOBOware:** The Onset desktop software used to program and download
  data from legacy UA-series HOBO loggers via optical USB coupler;
  also supports barometric compensation for water level loggers
  [@onset_hoboware].
- **Logging interval:** The time between successive measurements
  stored to the logger memory; typical intervals for EA Program
  deployments are 5 minutes (microclimatic studies) or 15 minutes
  (long-term monitoring); shorter intervals fill memory faster and
  require more frequent downloads [@onset_hobou23].
- **MX2301:** The Onset HOBO MX temperature and relative humidity
  logger; Bluetooth-enabled; ±0.2 °C temperature accuracy and ±2.5%
  RH accuracy; internal memory stores 500,000 readings [@onset_hobou23].
- **Radiation shield:** A ventilated, white polypropylene housing that
  surrounds a temperature or RH logger and prevents direct solar
  radiation from inflating the measured air temperature; a radiation
  shield is mandatory for any logger exposed to sunlight
  [@wmo_guide2018].
- **Relative humidity (RH):** The ratio of the partial pressure of
  water vapor in air to the saturation vapor pressure at the same
  temperature, expressed as a percentage; values above approximately
  70% promote sensor drift in some sensor types [@wmo_guide2018].
- **Sensor drift:** A gradual, systematic change in sensor readings
  over time not attributable to true environmental change; detected by
  co-deployment with a reference sensor or comparison with a nearby
  weather station.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Deployment may involve climbing, ladder use, or working
  on uneven terrain. Use a spotter when mounting loggers at height.
- **Environmental:** Heat exposure during summer deployments in
  Southern California. Carry adequate water and sun protection.
- **Wildlife:** Insects (bees, wasps), ticks, and snakes may be
  present at deployment sites.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling loggers at contaminated sites)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd).

|:----------|:-----------------|:-----------------------------|:-----------------------|:----------------|:--------------|
| MX2201    | Temp, light      | -20 to 70 °C; 0--320,000 lux | ±0.5 °C               | 96,000 readings | Bluetooth     |
| MX2202    | Temp, light (waterproof) | -20 to 70 °C          | ±0.5 °C               | 96,000 readings | Bluetooth     |
| MX2301    | Temp, RH         | -40 to 70 °C; 0--100% RH    | ±0.2 °C; ±2.5% RH     | 500,000 readings | Bluetooth    |

## Equipment and Materials

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| HOBO logger(s)                        | Confirm model and battery status         |
| Radiation shield (RS3 or similar)     | Required for temperature loggers exposed to direct sunlight [@wmo_guide2018] |
| Mounting hardware (cable ties, U-bolts, brackets) | For securing shield/logger to posts, trees, or tripods |
| Tripod or mounting post               | If no suitable tree or structure available |
| Smartphone with HOBOconnect app       | For Bluetooth-enabled MX loggers [@onset_hoboware] |
| Laptop with HOBOware software         | For legacy UA-series loggers [@onset_hoboware] |
| Optical USB coupler (for UA loggers)  | For launching and downloading            |
| Field notebook                        | For recording deployment metadata        |
| GPS unit or smartphone                | Per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd) |
| Spare batteries                       | CR2032 (MX pendant) or 3V lithium (varies by model) |


## Procedure

### Pre-Deployment Programming

**MX-series (Bluetooth):**

1. Open the HOBOconnect app and connect to the logger via Bluetooth
   [@onset_hoboware].
2. Configure:
   - Logging interval: 5 or 15 minutes
   - Start mode: delayed start (set to a round time, e.g., top of the
     next hour)
   - Logger name: use the convention `SiteID_Parameter_LoggerSN`
     (e.g., `BFS_TempRH_20456789`)
3. Verify the battery level. Replace if below 20%.

**UA-series (legacy):**

1. Connect the logger via the optical USB coupler and open HOBOware.
2. Select **Launch** and configure the logging interval and start time
   [@onset_hoboware].
3. Click **Start** to begin logging.

### Deployment

1. Mount the radiation shield at 1.5 m above ground on a post, tree,
   or tripod in a location representative of the site. Avoid positions
   within 3 m of heat-absorbing surfaces (pavement, metal walls)
   [@wmo_guide2018].
2. Insert the logger into the shield. Ensure the sensor faces are
   unobstructed and the shield ventilation holes are unblocked.
3. Secure the shield to the mounting structure with cable ties.
4. Record in the field notebook:
   - Logger serial number
   - Deployment coordinates per [SOP-F006](SOP-F006-gps-site-navigation.qmd)
   - Date and time of deployment
   - Logging interval and start time
   - Sensor height above ground
5. Photograph the deployed logger with surrounding context visible.

### Downloading Data at Regular Intervals

**MX-series (Bluetooth):**

1. Open HOBOconnect app and connect to the logger.
2. Select **Download** to transfer all stored data to the smartphone
   [@onset_hoboware].
3. Export the data as a CSV file.
4. Save using the naming convention:
   `YYYY-MM-DD_SiteID_Parameter_LoggerSN.csv`
5. Upload to the project GitHub repository under `data/microclimate/`
   within 48 hours.

**UA-series (legacy):**

Connect via optical USB coupler and use HOBOware to read out data.

### Logger Retrieval (End of Deployment)

1. Download all remaining data.
2. Remove the logger and mounting hardware.
3. Clean the logger housing with a damp cloth. For waterproof models,
   rinse with fresh water.
4. Inspect the radiation shield for damage; replace desiccant packs if
   applicable.
5. Store loggers in a dry, room-temperature location.


## Quality Control

- At each download visit, compare the logger temperature reading
  against a handheld thermometer. Discrepancies greater than 1 °C
  should be investigated [@wmo_guide2018].
- At least once per year, co-deploy two loggers of the same model at
  the same location for a minimum of 48 hours to check inter-unit
  agreement. Temperature should agree within 0.5 °C; RH within 5%.
- Inspect data for signs of sensor failure: constant readings, sudden
  offsets, or readings pegged at the sensor limit.
- Check battery level at every download. Replace batteries
  proactively if below 20%.
- For light loggers, verify that the sensor face has not shifted
  orientation by comparing the deployment photograph to current
  position.

## Training Record

Before deploying HOBO loggers independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Demonstrate logger programming via HOBOconnect or HOBOware
3. Participate in a supervised deployment including shield mounting
   and metadata recording
4. Demonstrate data download, export, and upload to the repository
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
